rules.contains:
They are not
  judged again, and their sentences are never listed as uncited.
A file several claims point into is shown once

A claim judged supported whose record still matches is
not handed to the judge again
Skip every hit in a file the diff touched.
A folder named through a shell variable is followed when the command assigns the variable or the environment holds it, and a command naming a variable with neither is let through.
- A comment the pattern scan wrote, which carries the pattern's own documented reason and fix.
- The draft, as a person will read it, without the comments the pattern scan or the test inventory wrote.

rules.absent: - The draft, as a person will read it.

rules.contains: Never edit or remove a comment the scan wrote.
Raise no finding that one of those patterns describes, since the scan already looked for it on every added line.
A comment the scan wrote is a finding under the check its header names, so that check's bullet opens with ❌ and links to it.
a comment on that line reading `symphony-allow: <pattern name>` excuses it from that one pattern
Paste what it prints as the Commits bullet, word for word.
The Commits bullet is pasted from a script, so it carries no claim.
A comment the test inventory wrote is treated exactly like one the scan wrote.
- A comment the test inventory wrote, which carries a finding about one test the pull request adds or changes.
Paste what it prints as the Conformance section, word for word, and name each unticked criterion in the verdict.
The Conformance section is pasted from a script, so it carries no claim.
A finding that changed code has behaviour no test reaches carries two claims: one pointing at that code, and one whose pointer is `{ "test_titles": true }`.
The capture resolves that pointer to every test title in the repo at the head commit, leaving out the tests the pull request adds that the test inventory found invalid.
- For a claim pointing at the test titles, the list of titles in place of a file. The claim says no test reaches a behaviour, and it is refuted when a listed title names that behaviour.
Every other claim is judged against the code captured for it, never against test titles.
A Tests finding that changed code has behaviour no test reaches carries a second claim, word for word the same sentence, whose pointer is `{ "test_titles": true }`.
